paragraphs.text: Now all the publicans and sinners were drawing near unto him to hear him.
paragraphs.original: Ἦσαν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες πάντες οἱ τελῶναι καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Ēsan de autō engizontes pantes hoi telōnai kai hoi hamartōloi akouein autou.

paragraphs.text: And both the Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διεγόγγυζον οἵ τε Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ἁμαρτωλοὺς προσδέχεται καὶ συνεσθίει αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai diegongyzon hoi te Pharisaioi kai hoi grammateis legontes hoti Houtos hamartōlous prosdechetai kai synesthiei autois.

paragraphs.text: And he spake unto them this parable, saying,
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de pros autous tēn parabolēn tautēn legōn·

paragraphs.text: What man of you, having a hundred sheep, and having lost one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?
paragraphs.original: Τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἔχων ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ ἀπολέσας ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν οὐ καταλείπει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ πορεύεται ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπολωλὸς ἕως εὕρῃ αὐτό;
paragraphs.translit: Tis anthrōpos ex hymōn echōn hekaton probata kai apolesas ex autōn hen ou kataleipei ta enenēkonta ennea en tē erēmō kai poreuetai epi to apolōlos heōs heurē auto;

paragraphs.text: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὑρὼν ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους αὐτοῦ χαίρων,
paragraphs.translit: kai heurōn epitithēsin epi tous ōmous autou chairōn,

paragraphs.text: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and his neighbors, saying unto them, Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον συγκαλεῖ τοὺς φίλους καὶ τοὺς γείτονας, λέγων αὐτοῖς· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὸ πρόβατόν μου τὸ ἀπολωλός.
paragraphs.translit: kai elthōn eis ton oikon synkalei tous philous kai tous geitonas, legōn autois· Syncharēte moi hoti heuron to probaton mou to apolōlos.

paragraphs.text: I say unto you, that even so there shall be joy in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, [more] than over ninety and nine righteous persons, who need no repentance.
paragraphs.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως χαρὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἔσται ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι ἢ ἐπὶ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα δικαίοις οἵτινες οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν μετανοίας.
paragraphs.translit: legō hymin hoti houtōs chara en tō ouranō estai epi heni hamartōlō metanoounti ē epi enenēkonta ennea dikaiois hoitines ou chreian echousin metanoias.

paragraphs.text: Or what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a lamp, and sweep the house, and seek diligently until she find it?
paragraphs.original: Ἢ τίς γυνὴ δραχμὰς ἔχουσα δέκα, ἐὰν ἀπολέσῃ δραχμὴν μίαν, οὐχὶ ἅπτει λύχνον καὶ σαροῖ τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ζητεῖ ἐπιμελῶς ἕως οὗ εὕρῃ;
paragraphs.translit: Ē tis gynē drachmas echousa deka, ean apolesē drachmēn mian, ouchi haptei lychnon kai saroi tēn oikian kai zētei epimelōs heōs hou heurē;

paragraphs.text: And when she hath found it, she calleth together her friends and neighbors, saying, Rejoice with me, for I have found the piece which I had lost.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὑροῦσα συγκαλεῖ τὰς φίλας καὶ γείτονας λέγουσα· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα.
paragraphs.translit: kai heurousa synkalei tas philas kai geitonas legousa· Syncharēte moi hoti heuron tēn drachmēn hēn apōlesa.

paragraphs.text: Even so, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως, λέγω ὑμῖν, γίνεται χαρὰ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs, legō hymin, ginetai chara enōpion tōn angelōn tou theou epi heni hamartōlō metanoounti.

paragraphs.text: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δέ· Ἄνθρωπός τις εἶχεν δύο υἱούς.
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de· Anthrōpos tis eichen dyo hyious.

paragraphs.text: and the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of [thy] substance that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ νεώτερος αὐτῶν τῷ πατρί· Πάτερ, δός μοι τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος τῆς οὐσίας· ὁ δὲ διεῖλεν αὐτοῖς τὸν βίον.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen ho neōteros autōn tō patri· Pater, dos moi to epiballon meros tēs ousias· ho de dieilen autois ton bion.

paragraphs.text: And not many days after, the younger son gathered all together and took his journey into a far country; and there he wasted his substance with riotous living.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μετʼ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας συναγαγὼν πάντα ὁ νεώτερος υἱὸς ἀπεδήμησεν εἰς χώραν μακράν, καὶ ἐκεῖ διεσκόρπισεν τὴν οὐσίαν αὐτοῦ ζῶν ἀσώτως.
paragraphs.translit: kai metʼ ou pollas hēmeras synagagōn panta ho neōteros hyios apedēmēsen eis chōran makran, kai ekei dieskorpisen tēn ousian autou zōn asōtōs.

paragraphs.text: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that country; and he began to be in want.
paragraphs.original: δαπανήσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο λιμὸς ἰσχυρὰ κατὰ τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤρξατο ὑστερεῖσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: dapanēsantos de autou panta egeneto limos ischyra kata tēn chōran ekeinēn, kai autos ērxato hystereisthai.

paragraphs.text: And he went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐκολλήθη ἑνὶ τῶν πολιτῶν τῆς χώρας ἐκείνης, καὶ ἔπεμψεν αὐτὸν εἰς τοὺς ἀγροὺς αὐτοῦ βόσκειν χοίρους·
paragraphs.translit: kai poreutheis ekollēthē heni tōn politōn tēs chōras ekeinēs, kai epempsen auton eis tous agrous autou boskein choirous·

paragraphs.text: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπεθύμει γεμίσαι τὴν κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν κερατίων ὧν ἤσθιον οἱ χοῖροι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδίδου αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai epethymei gemisai tēn koilian autou apo tōn keratiōn hōn ēsthion hoi choiroi, kai oudeis edidou autō.

paragraphs.text: But when he came to himself he said, How many hired servants of my father`s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish here with hunger!
paragraphs.original: εἰς ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἐλθὼν ἔφη· Πόσοι μίσθιοι τοῦ πατρός μου περισσεύονται ἄρτων, ἐγὼ δὲ λιμῷ ὧδε ἀπόλλυμαι·
paragraphs.translit: eis heauton de elthōn ephē· Posoi misthioi tou patros mou perisseuontai artōn, egō de limō hōde apollymai·

paragraphs.text: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight:
paragraphs.original: ἀναστὰς πορεύσομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ ἐρῶ αὐτῷ· Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου,
paragraphs.translit: anastas poreusomai pros ton patera mou kai erō autō· Pater, hēmarton eis ton ouranon kai enōpion sou,

paragraphs.text: I am no more worthy to be called your son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
paragraphs.original: οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου· ποίησόν με ὡς ἕνα τῶν μισθίων σου.
paragraphs.translit: ouketi eimi axios klēthēnai hyios sou· poiēson me hōs hena tōn misthiōn sou.

paragraphs.text: And he arose, and came to his father. But while he was yet afar off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἑαυτοῦ. ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος εἶδεν αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη καὶ δραμὼν ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai anastas ēlthen pros ton patera heautou. eti de autou makran apechontos eiden auton ho patēr autou kai esplanchnisthē kai dramōn epepesen epi ton trachēlon autou kai katephilēsen auton.

paragraphs.text: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight: I am no more worthy to be called thy son.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτῷ· Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου, οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho hyios autō· Pater, hēmarton eis ton ouranon kai enōpion sou, ouketi eimi axios klēthēnai hyios sou.

paragraphs.text: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth quickly the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ πρὸς τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ· Ταχὺ ἐξενέγκατε στολὴν τὴν πρώτην καὶ ἐνδύσατε αὐτόν, καὶ δότε δακτύλιον εἰς τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ὑποδήματα εἰς τοὺς πόδας,
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho patēr pros tous doulous autou· Tachy exenenkate stolēn tēn prōtēn kai endysate auton, kai dote daktylion eis tēn cheira autou kai hypodēmata eis tous podas,

paragraphs.text: and bring the fatted calf, [and] kill it, and let us eat, and make merry:
paragraphs.original: καὶ φέρετε τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν, θύσατε, καὶ φαγόντες εὐφρανθῶμεν,
paragraphs.translit: kai pherete ton moschon ton siteuton, thysate, kai phagontes euphranthōmen,

paragraphs.text: for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι οὗτος ὁ υἱός μου νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἀνέζησεν, ἦν ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη. καὶ ἤρξαντο εὐφραίνεσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: hoti houtos ho hyios mou nekros ēn kai anezēsen, ēn apolōlōs kai heurethē. kai ērxanto euphrainesthai.

paragraphs.text: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ πρεσβύτερος ἐν ἀγρῷ· καὶ ὡς ἐρχόμενος ἤγγισεν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, ἤκουσεν συμφωνίας καὶ χορῶν,
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de ho hyios autou ho presbyteros en agrō· kai hōs erchomenos ēngisen tē oikia, ēkousen symphōnias kai chorōn,

paragraphs.text: And he called to him one of the servants, and inquired what these things might be.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα τῶν παίδων ἐπυνθάνετο τί ἂν εἴη ταῦτα·
paragraphs.translit: kai proskalesamenos hena tōn paidōn epynthaneto ti an eiē tauta·

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἥκει, καὶ ἔθυσεν ὁ πατήρ σου τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν, ὅτι ὑγιαίνοντα αὐτὸν ἀπέλαβεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autō hoti Ho adelphos sou hēkei, kai ethysen ho patēr sou ton moschon ton siteuton, hoti hygiainonta auton apelaben.

paragraphs.text: But he was angry, and would not go in: and his father came out, and entreated him.
paragraphs.original: ὠργίσθη δὲ καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν εἰσελθεῖν. ὁ δὲ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐξελθὼν παρεκάλει αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ōrgisthē de kai ouk ēthelen eiselthein. ho de patēr autou exelthōn parekalei auton.

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, and I never transgressed a commandment of thine; and [yet] thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ· Ἰδοὺ τοσαῦτα ἔτη δουλεύω σοι καὶ οὐδέποτε ἐντολήν σου παρῆλθον, καὶ ἐμοὶ οὐδέποτε ἔδωκας ἔριφον ἵνα μετὰ τῶν φίλων μου εὐφρανθῶ·
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen tō patri autou· Idou tosauta etē douleuō soi kai oudepote entolēn sou parēlthon, kai emoi oudepote edōkas eriphon hina meta tōn philōn mou euphranthō·

paragraphs.text: but when this thy son came, who hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou killedst for him the fatted calf.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ὁ υἱός σου οὗτος ὁ καταφαγών σου τὸν βίον μετὰ πορνῶν ἦλθεν, ἔθυσας αὐτῷ τὸν σιτευτὸν μόσχον.
paragraphs.translit: hote de ho hyios sou houtos ho kataphagōn sou ton bion meta pornōn ēlthen, ethysas autō ton siteuton moschon.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that is mine is thine.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τέκνον, σὺ πάντοτε μετʼ ἐμοῦ εἶ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐμὰ σά ἐστιν·
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autō· Teknon, sy pantote metʼ emou ei, kai panta ta ema sa estin·

paragraphs.text: But it was meet to make merry and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive [again]; and [was] lost, and is found.
paragraphs.original: εὐφρανθῆναι δὲ καὶ χαρῆναι ἔδει, ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου οὗτος νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἔζησεν, καὶ ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη.
paragraphs.translit: euphranthēnai de kai charēnai edei, hoti ho adelphos sou houtos nekros ēn kai ezēsen, kai apolōlōs kai heurethē.
